name: fal.ai
description: Read-only fal.ai queue connector: poll the status and fetch the result of an async generation job (image, video, audio and 1000+ other models, all run through the same submit-then-poll queue). Submitting a job is a billable generation, so it is modelled write:true and HITL-gated and never fired in proof; the poll tools here are the zero-cost authed reads that satisfy the gate and that a Phase-B plugin would use to watch a submitted job finish.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Poll a submitted fal.ai job for its current queue status: queued, in progress, completed or failed, plus its queue position and the result URL once done. This is the ASYNC POLL half of the submit-then-poll pattern: submit_generation (write:true) starts a job and returns a request_id, this tool is the zero-spend authed read that checks on it. Also the spec's auth-proving test call

model_name.description: Model name within that owner's namespace, e.g. fast-sdxl

request_id.description: Job request id returned by submit_generation

tools.name: get_result
tools.description: Fetch the finished output of a completed fal.ai job: the generated images, video, audio or model-specific output. Reads an existing job only; it never starts a generation

model_name.description: Model name within that owner's namespace, e.g. fast-sdxl

request_id.description: Job request id returned by submit_generation

tools.name: submit_generation
tools.description: Submit a new generation job to a fal.ai model's async queue (image, video, audio, etc). This is the ASYNC SUBMIT half of the submit-then-poll pattern: it is a billable generation, so it is HITL-gated and never fired by the shape-proof harness. Poll the returned request_id with get_status once approved and started, then read the finished output with get_result

model_name.description: Model name within that owner's namespace, e.g. fast-sdxl

input.description: Model-specific input fields (prompt, image_size, etc), varies per model, see the model's own schema on fal.ai

needs_review: NO LIVE CREDENTIAL AT AUTHORING TIME, AND fal.ai HAS NO ZERO-SPEND LIVE READ EITHER: unlike Replicate, fal's poll endpoints need a real request_id, which needs a real (paid) submit first. This connector is expected to ship SHAPE_PROVEN or AUTH_WALL and stay that way until a Phase-B plugin can submit one cheap job (~$0.03) and poll it; do not claim LIVE_PROVEN for fal without a real submitted job, per the build plan.

MODEL ID SPLIT INTO owner + model_name (DEVIATION from the plan's single {{input.model_id}} placeholder): the shape-proof harness and the production declarative runtime both URL-encode every {{input.X}} path token (encodeURIComponent), which would turn a single 'fal-ai/fast-sdxl' value into 'fal-ai%2Ffast-sdxl' and break the real two-segment route. Split into separate owner/model_name inputs instead, mirroring replicate.connector.json's get_model(owner, name) shape, which has the same owner/name path structure and hit the same constraint. This covers the common 2-segment model id (the overwhelming majority of the catalogue, e.g. fal-ai/fast-sdxl); a handful of fal models publish deeper 3-segment ids (e.g. fal-ai/flux/dev) that this split cannot address without a third input field — flagged here rather than silently mishandled.

SUBMIT BODY IS WRAPPED, NOT A RAW PASSTHROUGH (a known Connector Spec v1 limitation): fal's real POST /{owner}/{model} expects the model's input parameters AT THE TOP LEVEL of the body with no wrapper key, but this factory's spec format has no primitive for 'the body IS this caller-supplied object' (request.body must be a JSON object of templated leaf values, per specSchema.js; there is no key-spread mechanism). submit_generation therefore sends {"input": {...}}, mirroring replicate's create_prediction shape rather than fal's actual wire contract. This is acceptable ONLY because submit_generation is write:true, HITL-gated, and never fired by shape-proof or by live-proof without --include-writes: nobody has exercised this body shape against the real API. A Phase-B plugin implementing real submission MUST send the model input object unwrapped at the top level, not what this declarative body literally produces; flagging so this is not silently trusted as tested.
AUTH HEADER: 'Authorization: Key <api_key>' (not Bearer) is the #1 fal integration mistake per the dossier; verified against docs.fal.ai 2026-09-16.

New vault credentialType 'fal' registered in integrationTypeRegistry.js (format-only test depth: testEndpoint is null because there is no cheap account/model-list GET, validateCredentials checks key length only).
